## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Paṭhamabhikkhādāyikāvimānavatthu* ("Alms Giver’s Mansion", Vv 27) is a poetic text preserved in the *Vimānavatthu* of the Pali Tipiṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The text recounts how a female deity (*devā*) explains the meritorious deeds of giving alms in her past life that resulted in her radiant celestial rebirth and beautiful physical form [SuttaCentral]. Five translations into modern languages are recorded on SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral].
No cross-language parallels in Sanskrit, Chinese, or Tibetan are recorded on SuttaCentral or identified by DharmaNexus [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. However, automated text-reuse analysis reveals extensive formulaic overlap within the Pali canon, identifying 187 shared passages across 27 canonical and post-canonical texts [DharmaNexus]. Besides extensive alignment with its commentary in the *Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā* and the *Petavatthu-aṭṭhakathā*, the text shares significant verse material with multiple other *Vimānavatthu* poems [DharmaNexus]. Its closest canonical alignments include the *Guttilavimānavatthu* (Vv 33), *Tiladakkhiṇavimānavatthu* (Vv 10), *Paṭhamasuṇisāvimānavatthu* (Vv 13), and its companion text, the *Dutiyabhikkhādāyikāvimānavatthu* (Vv 28, matching nearly the entirety of segments §0.1–7.1) [DharmaNexus].
*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
